subject: [Console] Request: route comparison + SLO-exception lane for high-cost flows
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Console] Request: route comparison + SLO-exception lane for high-cost flows

Hi team,

We're seeing an uptick in BrightEdge Tier customers surfacing questions about why certain chat endpoints spike cost even when token volumes look stable. Sara at BrightEdge asked for a per-route "cost delta" comparison so they can see which routes (and variants) are driving unexpected spend.

Quick ask: can Console expose a lightweight per-route comparison tile that shows, for a selected time window,
- token count vs billed token units (to catch accounting gaps)
- p50/p95 latency breakdown per model variant
- a delta column (% change week-over-week)

Secondary (higher priority for us): allow attaching an SLO-exception "lane" to the tile so customers can opt in to narrow alerts that only fire when cost-per-inference exceeds a configured threshold AND tail-latency is elevated. This would reduce noisy alerts while giving proactive visibility.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with an example layout and an anonymized high-cost trace. No need to build an advanced UI—MVP could be a table + sparkline and a single-rule exception builder.

Could Product + Instrumentation estimate effort and feasibility? If Platform needs to add an aggregation endpoint (per-route daily aggregates with variant dimension) say so — we can timebox the scope.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Manager, Observability Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-comparison-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet), example-high-cost-trace.har (trace)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Console] Request: route comparison + SLO-exception lane for high-cost flows

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments, very helpful. A couple quick clarification questions from Platform side before we scope:
1) Time window granularity: are you expecting hourly, 15-min, or daily buckets for the delta comparisons? Hourly increases storage/compute costs.
2) Variant dimension: do you need model-quantization/engine granularity (e.g., gpt-4x-8q vs gpt-4x-16q) or is model-family enough?
3) Exception lane semantics: should the exception be evaluated on aggregated route-level metrics (per minute) or on sample-level traces? Aggregated rules are cheaper but less precise.

Rough note: building a daily aggregated endpoint with p50/p95, token-billed mapping, and a week-over-week delta is straightforward (1 backend sprint + 1 infra sprint). Hourly would add ~50% to effort. UI tile + exception builder MVP is another 1 sprint if we keep controls minimal.

Happy to sync for 30 minutes.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff SRE, Serving Platform

Appreciate the context, Kim — and good notes Marcus.

Product perspective: this aligns with the roadmap theme "route economics visibility" for Q3. A few product priorities to capture:
- Impact: ease BrightEdge's renewals conversation (they flagged this in their CSM call).
- Safety: exception lanes should be tenant-config only, default OFF.
- UX: keep the tile queryable (time-range + compare-to window) and add a small explanation tooltip that maps "billed units" to tokens so customers don't conflate raw tokens with billing multipliers.

I'm going to slot this as a "small" cross-functional deliverable. Marcus, can you confirm the backend MVP estimate (daily vs hourly) by EOD? Jasmine, can you sketch a mock for the tile (table + sparkline + single-rule exception UI) — 2 quick wireframes are fine.

If estimates look like 2-3 sprints total, I'll add this to the Q3 cross-team plan and loop in Solutions/CS for early access.

Marissa

Quick mocks attached (two variants):
- compact table-first tile (good for dashboards)
- panel-first with expanded rule editor (good for detailed tenant page)

Notes: I've kept the exception rule builder to three fields: metric (cost-per-inference / p95-latency), threshold, evaluation window. Rule examples included in comments. For BrightEdge specifically, we should include a pre-built threshold template ("high-cost inference") so they can opt in quickly.

Marcus — for MVP let's go daily aggregates to keep infra effort low and get this in front of customers. If we see value, we can iterate to hourly for a subset of tenants.

Kimberly — can you send me Sara's sample query timespan (they usually look at 7d and month-over-month) so I can wire in the compare defaults?
